## A native terminal

- Terminals are now drawn natively instead of inside an embedded browser. Ghostty's terminal core (libghostty-vt) parses the output, and Direct2D and DirectWrite draw it straight into the window.
- Lighter and faster: a window with a terminal uses about 300 MB of memory instead of about 700 MB, and heavy output over SSH takes well under half the CPU it used to.
- Switching tabs is instant, with no gray flash while a terminal appears.
- Typing in Japanese, Chinese, Korean and other languages that use an input method editor now works in the terminal, as do the emoji panel (Win+.), voice typing (Win+H) and the touch keyboard.
- Text looks the way programs intend: curly, double, dotted and dashed underlines, underline colors (such as editor diagnostics), overlines, and bold text in bright colors.
- Alt+drag selects a rectangle, handy for columns of `show` output. Shift+click extends a selection.
- The mouse wheel scrolls in `less`, `man` and other full-screen programs. Touchpads scroll smoothly, Alt+wheel scrolls faster, and Ctrl+wheel zooms.
- Links open with a click, including links that programs mark up themselves.
- Setup no longer installs the Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime.

## Ruler and commands

- Hover anywhere on the ruler beside the scroll bar to see that line, when it arrived and how long ago, and the matches, bookmarks and highlights around it. Click anywhere on it to jump there.
- Rewind and recording playback show command marks.
- In a split, the ruler stays quieter in the group you are not using.
- Fixed command history sometimes recording an older command, with everything after it as its output, on servers without shell integration.

## Fixes and polish

- Buttons and dialogs have the native Windows look.
- Telnet sessions can keep the terminal at 80 columns, for BBS art and menus.
- The keyboard stays on the terminal after you open or close a tab.
- Tabs open, close and move with smoother, consistent motion.
- An unreadable sessions, SSH keys or highlights file is kept rather than replaced.
- Recording heavy output uses much less CPU.

Find no longer has match case and regular expression options. They will be back in a later release.

Choose the x64 download for Intel or AMD PCs. Choose ARM64 only for Windows on ARM devices.
